No shell commands, installations, candidate execution or trials occurred. The six proposed repositories all predate the 90-day window and each returned a default-branch commit since 2026-07-07. Weekly commit frequency, dependency advisories and publisher concentration were not measured. Stars and licenses did not influence ranking. The north-star action is reproducible, attributable evidence retrieval for US-equities historical simulation; no trading action is proposed.

The supplied winner evidence establishes local integration, not comparative superiority on a frozen source set. All three remain provisional controls. Current repository metadata shows the same canonical owners and unarchived status, with Apache-2.0 for [agent-browser](https://api.github.com/repos/vercel-labs/agent-browser) and MIT for [Tavily CLI](https://api.github.com/repos/tavily-ai/tavily-cli) and [OpenResearch](https://api.github.com/repos/alphaXiv/OpenResearch). [OpenResearch v0.2.15](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch/releases/tag/v0.2.15) adds literature-request retries, process cleanup, low-memory child release and native-model identity reporting. Neither release demonstrates superior source coverage. Tavily's package/release currency was not independently rechecked.

Client-native browser lanes belong in the comparison. [Claude's Chrome documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome) verifies --chrome, visible browser operation, shared login state, a direct Anthropic plan and /login requirements, and lack of WSL support. Correction to the simplified permission lead: the documentation also describes circumstances where auto-mode approval skips the extension's per-site check; pin permission mode and deny rules in tests. On Macs, compare this lane with agent-browser using synthetic accounts and identical tasks. For Codex, [v0.160.0 feature source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs) describes stable, default-enabled, requirements-only desktop browser gates. Installed --help and TUI behavior could not be checked, so exec/TUI availability remains unestablished rather than absent. No Mac lane was qualified here.

Injection comparisons should model an attacker controlling retrieved HTML, Markdown, indexes, redirects and tool-result content, with synthetic session data and canaries as protected assets. Measure unauthorized navigation, uploads, state changes and exfiltration attempts separately from answer corruption. [Playwright MCP's README](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp/blob/main/README.md) explicitly says origin filters do not bound redirects or constitute a security boundary; keep it as a comparison option, not an injection guard. The [IPI-proxy paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11868) verifies an approach that modifies real allowed-domain responses and tracks callbacks. Its repository identity and maintenance were not resolved within budget, so it remains pending. Promptfoo's template tests must not be presented as equivalent coverage.

Point-in-time capture and model hindsight are separate problems. [Look-Ahead-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13770) evaluates temporal bias in financial workflows; [HindsightBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18867) describes date-manipulation probes and sensitivity to serving configuration. Their abstracts justify a separate parametric-hindsight check, not a claim that dated retrieval removes model leakage. Model, quantization and reasoning settings should be fixed in that comparison. [Cloudflare's documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/markdown-for-agents/) verifies Accept: text/markdown negotiation and removal of ETag/Last-Modified during conversion. Which installed fetch lanes send that header remains unchecked; converted response metadata must not be assumed to establish historical vintage.
